name: Three Base Stations
description: The New Vasjuki village is stretched along the motorway and that's why every house on it is characterized by its shift relative to some fixed point — the x i coordinate. The village consists of n houses, the i -th house is located in the point with coordinates of x i . TELE3, a cellular communication provider planned to locate three base stations so as to provide every house in the village with cellular communication. The base station having power d located in the point t provides with communication all the houses on the segment [ t - d , t + d ] (including boundaries). To simplify the integration (and simply not to mix anything up) all the three stations are planned to possess the equal power of d . Which minimal value of d is enough to provide all the houses in the village with cellular communication.
input_specification: The first line contains an integer n ( 1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10 5 ) which represents the number of houses in the village. The second line contains the coordinates of houses — the sequence x 1 , x 2 , ..., x n of integer numbers ( 1 ≤ x i ≤ 10 9 ). It is possible that two or more houses are located on one point. The coordinates are given in a arbitrary order.
output_specification: Print the required minimal power d . In the second line print three numbers — the possible coordinates of the base stations' location. Print the coordinates with 6 digits after the decimal point. The positions of the stations can be any from 0 to 2·10 9 inclusively. It is accepted for the base stations to have matching coordinates. If there are many solutions, print any of them.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 51C — Three Base Stations [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
